args.body:
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT — TRACKED CHANGES REDLINE
Counterparty Draft vs. Firm Standard (Reconciled)

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
This redline incorporates all required modifications to the counterparty's draft agreement, addressing three material deviations identified in the counterparty's latest markup:
1. Indemnification cap reduction and basket restructuring
2. Material Adverse Effect definition carve-outs
3. Representation survival period shortening

All marked changes reflect positions negotiated against the firm's internal playbook and market-standard Account Control Agreement precedent.

---

SECTION 1: INDEMNIFICATION AND REMEDIES [TRACKED CHANGE]

FIRM STANDARD (Original):
"1.1 Indemnification Cap. The maximum aggregate liability under this indemnification provision shall not exceed $[5,000,000], subject to a deductible basket of $[100,000], below which no claims shall accrue."

COUNTERPARTY MARKUP (Deviation Identified):
"1.1 Indemnification Cap. The maximum aggregate liability under this indemnification provision shall not exceed $[3,500,000], subject to a tipping basket of $[150,000], above which all claims (including those below the basket) shall be fully recoverable."

FIRM REDLINE (Required Position):
"1.1 Indemnification Cap. The maximum aggregate liability under this indemnification provision shall not exceed $[5,000,000]¶ [DELETION: proposed reduction to $3,500,000 REJECTED], subject to a deductible basket of $[100,000]¶ [DELETION: counterparty tipping basket restructuring REJECTED — maintains deductible structure], below which no claims shall accrue."

RATIONALE:
- Indemnification cap must remain at $5,000,000 to match credit agreement and account control precedent
- Deductible basket (not tipping basket) is market standard; tipping baskets disproportionately increase exposure by making sub-basket claims recoverable once aggregate threshold is crossed
- Firm standard $100,000 deductible reflects account size, transaction volume, and risk allocation appropriate to this engagement

---

SECTION 2: DEFINITIONS — MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT [TRACKED CHANGE]

FIRM STANDARD (Original):
"2.1 Material Adverse Effect. A material adverse effect means any event, change, or effect that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the business, results of operations, condition (financial or otherwise), or assets of the parties to this Agreement.

Excluded from this definition:
(a) General economic conditions or market conditions affecting the banking or credit industries generally;
(b) Changes in law or regulatory policy of general applicability;
(c) Natural disasters or acts of God;
(d) Changes in credit markets or availability of credit."

COUNTERPARTY MARKUP (Deviation Identified):
"2.1 Material Adverse Effect. A material adverse effect means any event, change, or effect that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the business, results of operations, condition (financial or otherwise), or assets of the parties to this Agreement.

Excluded from this definition:
(a) General economic conditions or market conditions affecting the banking or credit industries generally;
(b) Changes in law or regulatory policy of general applicability;
(c) Natural disasters or acts of God;
(d) Changes in credit markets or availability of credit;
(e) [NEW CARVE-OUT] Any regulatory investigation, enforcement action, or review by any federal, state, or local banking regulator;
(f) [NEW CARVE-OUT] Any examination, supervision, or compliance review by any depository institution regulator."

FIRM REDLINE (Required Position):
"2.1 Material Adverse Effect. A material adverse effect means any event, change, or effect that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the business, results of operations, condition (financial or otherwise), or assets of the parties to this Agreement.

Excluded from this definition:
(a) General economic conditions or market conditions affecting the banking or credit industries generally;
(b) Changes in law or regulatory policy of general applicability [NOTE: Does not exclude targeted regulatory action against a specific party];
(c) Natural disasters or acts of God;
(d) Changes in credit markets or availability of credit;
(e) [DELETION: Proposed regulatory investigation carve-out REJECTED] [COUNTERPARTY POSITION NOTES: Counterparty seeks to exempt regulatory investigations and enforcement actions from MAE definition]
(f) [DELETION: Proposed depository regulator supervision carve-out REJECTED] [COUNTERPARTY POSITION NOTES: Counterparty seeks to exempt regulatory examination and supervision from MAE definition]

FIRM ALTERNATIVE LANGUAGE (if regulatory carve-out negotiation required):
(e) Any regulatory investigation, enforcement action, examination, or supervision that is not specifically directed at or materially adverse to the regulated party, or that relates to industry-wide supervisory initiatives of general applicability."

RATIONALE:
- Broad regulatory carve-outs are off-market and unacceptable in account control agreements
- Regulatory action targeting a specific party (particularly investigations or enforcement) materially affects creditworthiness and operational capacity
- The matters giving rise to this engagement involve regulatory oversight; carving out all regulatory action gutted the firm's ability to respond to material adverse changes in counterparty condition
- Firm standard allows general regulatory policy changes; does not excuse party-specific enforcement or investigation
- If counterparty presses on this issue, narrow alternative language provided above preserves firm protections while acknowledging general regulatory initiatives

---

SECTION 3: REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES — SURVIVAL [TRACKED CHANGE]

FIRM STANDARD (Original):
"3.1 Survival of Representations. All representations and warranties in this Agreement shall survive closing and shall remain in full force and effect for a period of [24 months] following the Effective Date, except:
(a) Representations regarding title and authority shall survive for [36 months];
(b) Tax representations shall survive until sixty days after expiration of applicable statute of limitations;
(c) Environmental and regulatory representations shall survive for [48 months]."

COUNTERPARTY MARKUP (Deviation Identified):
"3.1 Survival of Representations. All representations and warranties in this Agreement shall survive closing and shall remain in full force and effect for a period of [12 months] following the Effective Date [REDUCTION FROM 24 MONTHS], except:
(a) Representations regarding title and authority shall survive for [18 months] [REDUCTION FROM 36 MONTHS];
(b) Tax representations shall survive until sixty days after expiration of applicable statute of limitations;
(c) Environmental and regulatory representations shall survive for [24 months] [REDUCTION FROM 48 MONTHS]."

FIRM REDLINE (Required Position):
"3.1 Survival of Representations. All representations and warranties in this Agreement shall survive closing and shall remain in full force and effect for a period of [24 months] following the Effective Date [DELETION: Counterparty proposed reduction to 12 months REJECTED], except:
(a) Representations regarding title and authority shall survive for [36 months] [DELETION: Counterparty proposed reduction to 18 months REJECTED];
(b) Tax representations shall survive until sixty days after expiration of applicable statute of limitations [MAINTAINED];
(c) Environmental and regulatory representations shall survive for [48 months] [DELETION: Counterparty proposed reduction to 24 months REJECTED]."

RATIONALE:
- Account control agreements for credit facilities require extended survival periods to allow detection of material misrepresentations during active credit relationship
- 24-month standard survival aligns with executed credit agreement and account opening materials
- Regulatory and environmental representations require 48-month survival due to regulatory examination cycles (typically 12-24 months) plus remediation and follow-up periods
- 12-month survival period is insufficient to discover account-level misrepresentations, dormant liabilities, or regulatory issues
- Title and authority representations require 36-month survival to allow discovery during account tenure and wind-down
- Counterparty's compressed timeline appears designed to shield underlying condition issues; firm must reject

---

SECTION 4: CONDITIONS TO CLOSING [UNCHANGED]

All conditions to closing remain as drafted. No deviations identified by counterparty; maintained per firm standard.

---

SECTION 5: TERMINATION AND WIND-DOWN [UNCHANGED]

Termination provisions remain as drafted. No material deviations identified; maintained per firm standard.

---

SECTION 6: ACCOUNT OPERATION AND CONTROL [RECONCILED]

The counterparty's markup does not introduce material deviations to account operation provisions. Standard controls are maintained:
- Firm retains sole discretion over account withdrawals
- Counterparty covenant to deliver account statements and transaction records
- Depository bank standard form control language incorporated without deviation
- Account details (balance thresholds, reporting frequency, signatory authority) confirmed per credit agreement

---

SECTION 7: GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION [UNCHANGED]

Governing law, jurisdiction, and dispute resolution provisions remain unchanged per firm standard and executed credit agreement precedent.

---

SUMMARY OF TRACKED CHANGES

Deviation 1: Indemnification Cap & Basket Structure
├─ Counterparty Position: Cap reduced from $5M to $3.5M; deductible converted to tipping basket
├─ Firm Standard: $5M cap with $100K deductible basket
├─ Firm Redline: REJECT both modifications; maintain firm standard
├─ Risk Level: HIGH
└─ Business Impact: $1.5M additional exposure if tipping basket adopted; increased claims exposure

Deviation 2: Material Adverse Effect Definition
├─ Counterparty Position: Exempt all regulatory investigations, enforcement, examinations, and supervision
├─ Firm Standard: Exclude only general regulatory policy changes; not party-specific action
├─ Firm Redline: REJECT broad carve-outs; offer narrow alternative if negotiation required
├─ Risk Level: CRITICAL
└─ Business Impact: Complete loss of MAE remedy for regulatory issues; unacceptable given engagement context

Deviation 3: Representation Survival Periods
├─ Counterparty Position: Reduce all survival periods by 50% (12m vs. 24m; 18m vs. 36m; 24m vs. 48m)
├─ Firm Standard: 24m general, 36m title/authority, 48m regulatory/environmental
├─ Firm Redline: REJECT all reductions; maintain firm standard periods
├─ Risk Level: HIGH
└─ Business Impact: Inadequate time to discover misrepresentations; regulatory issues may emerge post-survival

---

INSTRUCTIONS FOR NEGOTIATION

If counterparty presses on any deviation:

1. INDEMNIFICATION CAP: Stand firm on $5M cap and deductible basket structure. Market precedent strongly supports this position. Offer to adjust cap based on account size/transaction volume only if depository bank agreement permits and credit agreement is amended accordingly. Do not accept tipping basket.

2. MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT: Reject broad regulatory carve-outs. Offer compromise language at Section 2 above (treating only general regulatory initiatives, not party-specific action, as exclusions). This preserves firm protections while acknowledging market-standard exceptions.

3. REPRESENTATION SURVIVAL: Stand firm on all survival periods. These are standard in account control agreements and necessary to allow discovery of account-level issues during credit facility tenure. Offer to add sunset provision (e.g., "provided that no claim shall be brought after [date]") if counterparty seeks hard deadline, but do not reduce base survival periods.

---

END REDLINE
